title: Rollback playbook for content-moderation and LLM degradation (working draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, actionable rollback playbook focused on two tightly related failure modes we keep seeing in early LLM rollouts: (1) content-moderation regressions (false negatives / unsafe outputs) and (2) progressive quality degradation (model hallucination / prompt drift) that emerges after a canary or A/B sweep. Goal is to give ops, oncall, product PMs and SREs a single place for fast decisions, tests to run, and communication steps when we need to quickly revert an activation or reduce exposure.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: rollout steward, oncall SRE, product owner, trust & safety lead, solutions engineer serving the customer.
- Applies to: host API features, routing/traffic-slicing changes, model variant swaps, and prompt/template updates that are live behind canaries or A/B gates.
- Not covered: deep model training fixes, long-term model re-evals (see CON-9876).

High level strategy (three levers):
1) Traffic gating (immediate, non-invasive): reduce slice exposure to 0% or route affected cohort to a safe fallback model.
2) Config rollout rollback (quick): revert prompt/template change + redeploy routing rules (console rollback).
3) Model variant fallback (safe default): switch to previously-verified model id / quantization profile.
Use the least-disruptive lever possible; escalate to full revert only when safety signals persist.

When to consider rollback (signal matrix) - initial triage checklist:
- Safety signal indicators (immediate):
  - Spike in moderation rejects flagged by T&S automation (>5x baseline for same cohort)
  - Customer escalations reporting unsafe content (>=2 independent reports within a 30 min window)
  - Manual review sample shows true unsafe outputs (>=3 failures in random n=50)
- Quality/regression indicators (progressive):
  - A/B primary metric drop >5% relative to control sustained for 15+ minutes (relevant metric: helpfulness-score, conversion, CTR)
  - Latency/timeout increase correlated with model variant change (>2x P95 vs baseline)
  - Token cost spike with no commensurate quality improvement (>20% cost increase)
- Operational health signals: increased error rates (5xx), KV cache eviction spikes, GPU OOMs for new variant.

Immediate oncall play (first 10 minutes) - quick checklist:
- Page the oncall SRE and product steward: PagerDuty tag: LLM-ROLLBACK.
- Post initial incident note in #incidents and start a lightweight incident doc (link to incident template).
- Snapshot canary cohort traffic: console -> Routing -> Export slice -> timestamp.
- If mod-signal present, set slice exposure to 0% OR route slice to model: redwood-v1-safe (fast path).
- If regression (quality/latency) suspected, divert 100% of affected canary traffic to previous model variant.
- Run a quick manual sample: take 20 recent queries from canary and evaluate against moderation heuristics and golden prompts.

Commands & console quick actions (examples):
- Routing -> slice -> set exposure = 0% (action: pause-slice)
- Rollback model variant: console -> deployment -> revertTo("deployment-2025-01-20-03")
- Emergency fallback route: add policy: IF slice.name == "canary-x" THEN route = "redwood-v1-safe" PRIORITY=1000
- Gradual reduce: set exposure = 10% -> monitor 5 minutes -> 0% if still failing.

Communications (who to notify immediately):
- T&S (trust-and-safety@redwood) and product PM (owner)
- Customer success if impacted customers: @cs-lead + named CSMs for active pilots
- Solutions engineering on call to support rollback testing and customer repros
- Legal only if any PII/exfiltration suspected
Make a short public post in #incidents with: what happened, immediate action taken, where traffic is routed now, and next checkpoint time.

Decision matrix (short):
- Safety-failure (automated moderation): pause slice -> fallback model -> open incident -> full rollback if fallback fails.
- Quality fall (A/B metric): revert to control model variant for that slice, keep canary paused until root cause analysis.
- Latency/cost: throttle slice and revert or tune batching/seq-len config; only roll back if SLOs breach.

Post-rollback verification (15–60 min):
- Run 100-sample smoke against previously failing prompts (SRE + T&S) and confirm <1% failure rate.
- Check telemetry: latency P95, token_rate, moderations/sec back to baseline.
- Confirm customer rep(s) see improvement (if customer reported).

Postmortem and next steps (owner: product steward):
- Create incident postmortem within 48 hours. Minimum sections: timeline, impact, immediate actions, root cause hypothesis, next actions, verification plan.
- If a model variant caused the issue: add to blacklist for automated rollouts until an eval passes for the relevant prompt set.
- Update rollouts checklist and console default fallback mapping.

A/B experiment considerations (special cases):
- If A/B control is affected by safety drift: immediately quarantine the treatment arm and convert metrics to diagnostic-only until fixed.
- Preserve experiment integrity: do not swap traffic across treatment/control without re-randomization. Instead, stop treatment and mark experiment paused.
- Re-run offline statistical equivalence checks on pre-exposure segments before resuming.

Runbook exercises (recommended ops rehearsals):
- Quarterly tabletop with T&S + SRE + oncall: simulate a content regression in a staged canary and measure median time-to-pause.
- Chaos test: synthetic unsafe prompts injected into canary stream to validate detection and automatic fallback routing. (GH PR: #432 contains harness).

Known gaps / TODO (notes to self):
- We need a one-click rollback button in Console that reverts routing + model variant + prompt template together. Filed: ENG-1423 (priority med).
- Define SLA for CSM/customer notification (target: 30 min for enterprise pilots).
- Add preconfigured evaluation set per customer for faster verification (ideas in CON-9876).
- Integration test that simulates KV cache pressure when variant switching occurs — current tests are thin.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Should fallback model always be a quantized, conservative safety-tuned model or vary by customer tier? (ops tradeoffs: latency vs safety)
- Auto-reversion threshold: do we allow an automatic revert after X failed samples, or keep manual guard? (propose X=10 true failures in 30m)

Appendix: quick checklist (one-line for pager):
1) Acknowledge incident + post to #incidents
2) Pause slice OR route to safe model
3) Snapshot traffic and export recent requests
4) Run manual 20-sample check + T&S quick eval
5) Communicate to CSM + customer if needed
6) Open incident postmortem ticket and assign owner

References and links:
- Incident template: /confluence/incidents/llm-incident-template
- Related engineering ticket: ENG-1423 (console rollback UX)
- Safety evaluation guidelines: /confluence/t-s/eval-guidelines
- GH PR for canary harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/432

Quick narrative (two-sentence summary for execs):
We aim to ensure canaries and narrow A/B rollouts can be paused or reverted within minutes with clear human-in-loop checks. This playbook gives cross-functional owners a prioritized set of actions to reduce exposure, verify fixes, and communicate clearly to customers and stakeholders.

Handy contacts (short):
- Oncall SRE rotation: @oncall-sre
- Product steward: Sofia Chen (sofia@redwood.com)
- Trust & Safety: t-s@redwood.com
- PagerDuty: LLM-ROLLBACK escalation policy

End notes: this is a working draft — please add field notes from real incidents here, especially timing metrics (TTD, TTR) and sample prompts.
